answer: In a Wesolowski time-lock, each identity must perform a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings before producing a proof that others can verify cheaply. GPUs may run separate clone chains in parallel, but cannot collapse the dependency between squarings in any one chain into a faster parallel computation. Thus each clone still incurs a physical delay and computation cost, imposing a per-identity bottleneck—not an absolute bar on well-resourced Sybil attacks. Like a lotus crossing a dune to reach a jetty, each chain must pass through its steps in order.
